question: What is a business cycle? Explain the different phases of a business cycle.

points.label: Meaning
points.description: A business cycle is the recurring rise and fall of overall economic activity (output, income, employment) over time; cycles are recurrent but not regular in length or intensity.

points.label: Expansion
points.description: Output, employment, income, demand, investment and prices rise; business confidence and credit grow.

points.label: Peak
points.description: The highest point of activity; resources are fully used, costs and prices are high and growth begins to slow, marking the upper turning point.

points.label: Contraction
points.description: Activity declines: demand, output, employment, investment and profits fall; when severe it is called a recession or depression.

points.label: Trough and recovery
points.description: The trough is the lowest point, with high unemployment and low demand; recovery follows as demand, investment and employment slowly pick up, leading to a new expansion.
